bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Saras Mela 2026 Begins in Patna - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Saras Mela 2026 Begins in Patna 22 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar Saras Mela 2026 began at Gyan Bhawan, Patna , bringing together rural women entrepreneurs, artisans and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from more than 15 States . The 10-day event aims to provide rural women with wider market access and promote their products, skills and entrepreneurship. Key Points: Organiser: The fair is organised by JEEViKA under the Rural Development Department, Government of Bihar . Venue and Duration: The event is being held at Gyan Bhawan, Patna , and will continue for 10 days , from 20 to 29 September 2026 . Participation: Women entrepreneurs and SHG members from Bihar and 14 other States are participating, showcasing regional products, crafts and traditional food. Products Displayed: The fair features handicrafts, handlooms, folk art, Madhubani paintings, khadi products, bamboo and wooden articles, silk items, jewellery, traditional foods, pickles, papad and sattu , among others. Market Linkages: A major focus is on connecting rural producers with urban and national markets , enabling women entrepreneurs to understand consumer preferences and expand their businesses. Buyer-Seller Interaction: The 2026 edition includes direct interaction between potential/institutional buyers and women entrepreneurs on product quality, packaging, quantity, supply capacity and market demand . JEEViKA: The programme is an important part of Bihar's rural livelihood ecosystem, supporting women through Self-Help Groups, savings, formal banking, credit and livelihood activities . Didi Ki Rasoi: Women associated with JEEViKA also participate through Didi Ki Rasoi , which provides hygienic and affordable food in institutions such as hospitals, schools and government establishments. Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana: According to the Rural Development Minister, more than 1.85 crore women have benefited from the scheme. Biharika Brand: The fair also saw the launch of a new logo for Biharika , the collective brand associated with products made by Bihar's rural women entrepreneurs. bihar_raw_news.title: 'No point in talking about big schemes if women are not safe': Priyanka Gandhi on Jamui case
bihar_raw_news.content: 'No point in talking about big schemes if women are not safe': Priyanka Gandhi on Jamui case Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra condemned the alleged harassment of two minors in Bihar's Jamui and said governments must ensure women's safety in public spaces. She also spoke about her ongoing visit to Wayanad and her plans to understand constituency-level issues. ANI | Updated: 22-09-2026 13:43 IST | Created: 22-09-2026 13:43 IST Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra (Photo/ ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Tuesday expressed concern over the alleged harassment of two minors in Bihar's Jamui, saying that crimes against women were increasing and that governments must ensure their safety in public spaces. "It's horrible. Crimes against women are just increasing. It's become unsafe for women. It was always unsafe, but it's become more and more increasingly violent towards women. I think that there's no point in talking about big schemes and programs if we can't even ensure the safety of women on our streets. So it's really something that all of us need to think about. Wherever there are state governments and especially the central government, they need to think about how they are going to ensure that women feel safe," Priyanka Gandhi said. Her remarks came after a video purportedly showing the alleged harassment and assault of two minors in Bihar's Jamui surfaced on social media, triggering public outrage and political reactions. Police have registered a case under relevant provisions, including the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, and arrested three people in connection with the incident. An SIT has also been formed to identify and apprehend the remaining suspects. The incident reportedly took place on September 19, when the two teenagers were returning from coaching classes. According to reports, a group of people stopped and allegedly harassed the minors, with portions of the incident being recorded and subsequently circulated online. The case has prompted criticism from Opposition leaders, who have raised questions over women's safety and law and order in Bihar. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi condemned the incident and called for those involved to be identified and prosecuted under the POCSO Act. The National Commission for Women has also taken suo motu cognisance of the incident and sought action from the Bihar Police, including the identification and arrest of those allegedly involved. Authorities have separately initiated action against social media accounts circulating footage that could reveal the identities of the minors. Speaking about her ongoing visit to Wayanad, Priyanka Gandhi said that she hoped to meet as many people as possible and understand local issues in detail. "I'm here, and I hope this is a longer trip. I hope to meet as many people as I can and, as always, to understand the issues in depth so that I can take proper action about them," she said. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM reviews ' Bihar Gati' projects; directs launch of Gaya IMC by mid-October
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM reviews 'Bihar Gati' projects; directs launch of Gaya IMC by mid-October ANI | Updated: Sep 22, 2026 16:10 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], September 22 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday chaired a high-level review meeting at the 'Sankalp' auditorium to assess the progress of mega infrastructure and welfare projects valued at over Rs 100 crore under the 'Bihar Gati' initiative, along with other centrally sponsored and state schemes. During the meeting, the Chief Minister directed officials to fast-track all ongoing development works, maintain high quality standards, and ensure completion within stipulated deadlines through strict inter-departmental coordination and regular monitoring. Key departments reviewed during the session included Road Construction, Water Resources, Industries, and Social Welfare. Department secretaries—including Pankaj Kumar Pal (Road Construction), Chandrashekhar Singh (Water Resources), Kundan Kumar (Industries), and Vinod Singh Gunjiyal (Social Welfare)—briefed the Chief Minister on the current status of their respective projects. Reviewing industrial infrastructure, the Chief Minister directed the Industries Department to operationalise the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) in Gaya, being developed under the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC), by the second week of October. The project is projected to attract industrial investments worth approximately Rs 20,000 crore to the state. Officials were instructed to complete the required support infrastructure and utilities in a time-bound manner. Reviewing schemes run by the Social Welfare Department and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), including Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti-Samarthya, and nutrition schemes for adolescent girls, the Chief Minister issued strict directives to release all pending honorariums of Anganwadi and associated frontline workers before the upcoming Durga Puja festival. He emphasised that the benefits of women and child development schemes must reach targeted beneficiaries without administrative delays. The Chief Minister reviewed key road connectivity projects, specifically directing the Road Construction Department to prepare a detailed plan to widen the Sultanganj-Tarapur-Sangrampur-Belhar-Katoria-Chandan-Dardmara route. He instructed officials to develop the section from 0.0 km to 40.0 km into a four-lane highway and ensure four-lane construction on the stretch from Belhar to Dardmara to cater to future traffic demands. Directives were also issued to expedite urban drinking water supply projects for Aurangabad, Sasaram, and Dehri, which rely on the surface water of the Sone River. The Chief Minister stressed that there must be no laxity in providing quality potable water to citizens. Additionally, the Water Resources Department was instructed to speed up construction work on the barrage over the Kamla River in Jaynagar, Madhubani district, to ensure timely irrigation benefits for local farmers. The meeting also explored clean energy initiatives, with the Chief Minister directing officials to prepare a feasibility study and comprehensive action plan for the solarisation of canals and river embankments across South Bihar. The meeting was attended by Principal Secretary to CM Deepak Kumar, Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh, Additional Chief Secretary (Environment, Forest & Climate Change) Anand Kishore, along with secretaries of energy, sports, revenue, and other senior officials. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy -2026 may attract Rs 16000 crore investment, create 12000 jobs
bihar_raw_news.content: Home All News Green Hydrogen Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy-2026 may attract Rs 16,000 crore investment, create 12,000... All News Green Hydrogen Bihar Green Hydrogen Policy-2026 may attract Rs 16,000 crore investment, create 12,000 jobs By Randhir Patil September 22, 2026 AI Representational Image Patna: Bihar is preparing to enter the green hydrogen sector with a proposed policy that could bring in investments of around Rs 16,000 crore and create nearly 12,000 jobs, as the state government steps up efforts to develop production, consumption and supporting infrastructure, according to an official following a high-level review meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Monday, The Times of India reported. Choudhary reviewed the draft policy at the ‘Sankalp’ auditorium in Lok Sevak Awas and directed officials to accelerate Bihar’s entry into the green hydrogen sector. Officials of Bihar State Power Holding Company Ltd presented a roadmap for developing a green hydrogen economy in the state, covering production and consumption targets, incentives, implementation measures and the infrastructure required to support the sector. During the meeting, Choudhary directed officials to promote green hydrogen production, consumption and investment across Bihar and develop the necessary infrastructure. He also asked power sector officials to coordinate with Barauni Refinery and Hindustan Urvarak Rasayan Limited (HURL) to examine the feasibility of setting up hydrogen plants at other locations in the state. The chief minister further directed officials to prepare an action plan in consultation with industries and institutions concerned, taking into account Bihar’s potential for green hydrogen production and utilisation. Choudhary said Bihar should align its green hydrogen initiatives with the National Green Hydrogen Mission-2030 to promote clean energy, green technology and sustainable development. He directed officials to link efforts to increase green hydrogen production and consumption with national targets so that the state can benefit from emerging opportunities in the sector. The meeting also reviewed the National Green Hydrogen Mission’s targets for 2030, the potential for green hydrogen production and consumption in Bihar and key provisions of the proposed state policy. The National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to develop at least 5 million metric tonnes of annual green hydrogen production capacity in India by 2030. Bihar Energy Minister Shailesh Kumar, also known as Bulo Mandal, Energy Department Secretary Ajay Yadav and senior power sector officials attended the meeting. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna HC Orders Bihar to Give Prisoners Remission Records, Hearing Before Forfeiture and ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna High Court directs Bihar to ensure transparency in remission records, hearing before deduction, grievance mechanisms and safeguards for prisoners under the Bihar Prison Manual. Advertisement Join WhatsApp Join Telegram The Patna High Court has issued a series of directions and recommendations to improve the remission and premature-release framework for prisoners in Bihar. The Division Bench examined how ordinary and special remission is calculated, whether the existing system permits selective treatment, and whether the Bihar Prison Manual, 2012 gives excessive discretion to prison authorities. The judgment was delivered in suo motu proceedings registered pursuant to the Supreme Court's order dated November 4, 2025, in SLP (Crl.) No. 529 of 2021. Advertisement The Court framed five questions concerning the calculation of ordinary remission, the functioning of the Remission Committee, special remission under Rules 428 and 429, the position of prisoners without education or vocational training, and the extent of executive discretion under the Bihar Prison Manual. The Bench comprising Justice Bibek Chaudhuri and Justice Chandra Shekhar Jha considered written submissions from the parties and assistance from Amicus Curiae Advocate Pratik Kumar Sinha. The Court explained that eligible convicted prisoners can earn ordinary remission based on conduct and work. Under the Manual, two days may be earned each month for good conduct and participation in institutional activities, another two days for prescribed work, and one additional day for certain work performed on Sundays and holidays. The maximum ordinary remission is seven days in a month and 84 days in a year. Advertisement The Court also directed that prisoners must receive a duplicate copy of their History Ticket showing remission earned or forfeited. "We direct that henceforth every prisoner shall be supplied with a duplicate copy of the History Ticket reflecting the remission earned or forfeited, so that the prisoner is fully informed and can seek rectification if necessary." The Bench held that the executive's discretion in remission matters is subject to safeguards. While the existing rules were not found to be "absolutely selective" or to confer excessive and unbridled power, the Court stressed transparency, reasoned decisions and natural justice. In particular, before remission already granted is deducted or seized, the prisoner must be given an opportunity of hearing and a reasoned order must follow. The Court noted that special remission under Rule 428 is available to all convicted prisoners without an educational qualification. However, Rule 429 provides an additional incentive to long-term prisoners who assist in improving educational standards or imparting vocational training. Advertisement To address possible inequality, the Court directed the State to examine whether an alternative route could be created for illiterate prisoners to earn comparable additional remission through other reformative or institutional contributions. The Court recommended fixed timelines for premature-release proceedings, including initiating the process at least six months before the eligibility date. It also recommended mechanisms for correcting remission calculations, appeals against seizure, and greater transparency regarding life convicts' remission and premature-release cases. bihar_raw_news.title: 84 lakh women to benefit from Vettri Payanam scheme daily - The New Indian Express
bihar_raw_news.content: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay chairing a review meeting on the rollout of expanded free bus travel scheme at the secretariat on Monday Photo | Express Tamil Nadu 84 lakh women to benefit from Vettri Payanam scheme daily The integration of the buses covered under ‘Vettri Payanam’ with electronic ticketing machines (ETMs) has been completed. Express News Service Updated: 22nd Sep, 2026 at 8:36 AM CHENNAI: Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday chaired a meeting at the secretariat to review the preparations for launching the expanded free bus travel scheme for women, ‘Vettri Payanam’, on October 2. Under ‘Vettri Payanam’, the facility will be expanded to Express, Limited stop service and Deluxe buses operating in cities and towns, Mofussil Ordinary buses and Ghat Ordinary buses operating on hill routes beyond 40 km. A total of 12,692 buses will be brought under the scheme, benefiting around 84.32 lakh women every day. The integration of the buses covered under ‘Vettri Payanam’ with electronic ticketing machines (ETMs) has been completed. Testing and verification are scheduled to be completed by September 25, while trial runs will be conducted on September 27. As the model code of conduct is in effect in Chengalpattu and Tiruppur districts for bypolls to Madurantakam and Dharapuram seats, the scheme will be implemented in these districts once the MCC is lifted. bihar_raw_news.title: TN launches solar subsidy scheme , targets 1 lakh homes - The New Indian Express
bihar_raw_news.content: Minister Nirmal Kumar launches TN Rooftop Solar Subsidy Scheme at a function held in Chennai on Monday Photo | P Jawahar Tamil Nadu TN launches solar subsidy scheme, targets 1 lakh homes Under the scheme, consumers eligible for the centre’s subsidy from August 5, 2026, will receive an additional subsidy from the state government. Express News Service Updated: 22nd Sep, 2026 at 6:55 AM CHENNAI: Energy and Law Minister C T R Nirmal Kumar launched the Tamil Nadu Rooftop Solar Subsidy Scheme and the new rooftop solar portal at the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board (TNEB) headquarters on Monday, and announced a target to cover one lakh homes by March 2027. Under the scheme, consumers eligible for the centre’s subsidy from August 5, 2026, will receive an additional subsidy from the state government. The combined subsidy will be Rs 35,000 for rooftop solar systems up to 1 kW, Rs 70,000 for systems up to 2 kW and up to Rs 1 lakh for systems up to 3 kW. He said, “Once the central subsidy is credited, the state portal will automatically process and release the additional state subsidy. Consumers will not have to submit a separate application.” Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on August 5 announced that the state has allocated Rs 50 crore this financial year for the subsidy. “If demand exceeds the target, additional funds and subsidy support will be sought with the CM’s approval,” the minister said. The newly launched portal will provide information on rooftop solar schemes, central and state subsidies, installation procedures, application status and empanelled solar agencies. It will also integrate procedures related to applications, solar installation and meter connections, the minister explained. The minister said delays in meter installation will also be monitored through the integrated system. There is no shortage of meters, he said, adding that consumers can track their application status on the new portal (tnebltd.gov.in). However, implementation of the scheme in Tiruppur district’s Dharapuram and Chengalpattu district’s Madurantakam Assembly constituencies will be in abeyance until the Model Code of Conduct imposed for the October 6 by-elections is withdrawn. bihar_raw_news.title: Objections mount over draft KU rules restricting campus politics | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 21, 2026 Objections mount over draft KU rules restricting campus politics Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Objections have mounted against a draft Kerala University Students’ Code of Conduct Regulations that propose restrictions on political activities on campus and at affiliated colleges, even as university officials say nothing has been finalised or implemented. The university syndicate recently considered the draft regulations, which include restrictions on student organisations conducting protests, dharnas, recruiting new members, putting up posters and graffiti on walls, soliciting funds, organising events featuring political personalities and conducting online campaigning, according to members of the Left-aligned Kerala University Employees’ Union. Union members said the draft gives heads of departments on the university campus and principals of affiliated colleges powers to take action, including suspension, against students found violating the proposed rules. They said students involved in violent activities could face a one-year suspension, while proposed penalties include Rs 5,000 for students, Rs 10,000 for political organisations and Rs one lakh for repeated violations. Unpaid fines would be treated as arrears and could lead to procedures including revenue recovery and potential property attachment, withholding of examination results and criminal proceedings under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. The Kerala University Employees’ Union has opposed the proposed regulations, saying they are an attempt to restrict political activities on campuses and are undemocratic. The union said it will launch protests if the regulations are implemented, alleging that such restrictions would curtail students’ participation in organisational activities. Resmi R, Registrar of Kerala University, told PTI on Sunday that only a draft has been prepared and it is yet to be finalised. “The syndicate meeting discussed the Code of Conduct Regulations and only a draft based on a similar code at MG University, Kottayam, and a High Court order has been prepared. The final code will be brought out only after discussions with stakeholders, including students,” she said. She said no order has been issued to implement the proposed regulations. Meanwhile, Leader of the Opposition in the Keralam Assembly, Pinarayi Vijayan, condemned the proposed restrictions on student organisations on campuses, saying attempts to drive politics and political awareness out of campuses stemmed from a fear of a generation that asks questions. In a Facebook post on Saturday night, Vijayan said the decision appeared to be part of an agenda of those disturbed by student movements that had emerged across the country. “If those behind this anti-democratic decision do not withdraw from it, Keralam is certain to witness strong protests,” he said. Vijayan said the Constitution gives every citizen who turns 18 the right to vote and participate in choosing governments, and argued that denying young people the right to think politically, organise and respond while studying in educational institutions was unconstitutional and amounted to complete depoliticisation. national_raw_news.content: Vice President C P Radhakrishnan today inaugurated 9th India International Water Week 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, he stressed the precise usage of water and highlighted that it should be conserved. He underlined that Water Week is a significant platform to bring all stakeholders to deliberate upon the processing challenges of water management. He said that no single institution, sector or State can address the challenges related to water in isolation and called upon greater cooperation and a coordinated approach. Vice President further emphasised the need for a multi-stakeholder and multi-dimensional approach that brings together technological innovation, sound policy, scientific knowledge, local experience and community participation. He said such cooperation must extend across administrative and geographical boundaries to ensure sustainable, equitable and effective management of water resources. Mr Radhakrishnan said that climate change is making rainfall patterns increasingly uncertain, necessitating systems capable of managing both periods of excessive rainfall and prolonged dry spells. He stressed that river-basin management, groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and efficient irrigation must work together as part of an integrated approach to water management. Jal Shakti Minister C.R Patil highlighted the importance of water conservation and said that government is committed in providing safe and sufficient drinking water to every citizen in the country. He said that Water is a shared resource, and therefore, water security is also a shared responsibility. The theme of this year’s water week is Climate Resilient Water Management. The five-day international event will provide a multidisciplinary platform bringing together policymakers, global water leaders, experts, researchers, practitioners, industry, civil society and young professionals for dialogue, knowledge exchange, innovation and partnerships towards addressing emerging water challenges and advancing a water-secure and climate-resilient future.

national_raw_news.title: 26 mins ago | National 150 HM Amit Shah inaugurates National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force Heads in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today inaugurated the 3rd National Conference of Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) Heads of States and UTs in New Delhi. The two day conference serves as a powerful platform to safeguard future generations from the menace of drugs. Heads of ANTFs from 36 States and Union Territories are attending the conference, being organised by the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). Based on the theme of the United Resolve, Shared Responsibility, the conference is focussing on progress of targets assigned to State and UTs ANTFs in recently released Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-29). During the event, Union Home Minister Amit Shah also launched the new website of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB). He released four Television Commercials to create awareness among people about drug abuse. Mr Shah also laid the foundation stones for the new zonal office and residential complex of the NCB in Lucknow and a new zonal office complex in Dehradun. During the conference, deliberations will also focus on identifying and adopting appropriate strategies to further strengthen the Central Government’s measures for supply reduction, demand reduction, and harm reduction. The discussions are expected to generate actionable strategies to further strengthen drug law enforcement and keep the youth of the country away from drugs. Union Home Ministry said that Central government is working in mission mode to protect the nation’s youth from the adverse effects of drug abuse. The Ministry said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has set the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, and realising this vision is not possible without building a drug-free India.

national_raw_news.title: 28 mins ago | National 302 President Droupadi Murmu to present 72nd National Film Awards in Gujarat today
national_raw_news.content: Marking a new chapter in Indian cinema, President Droupadi Murmu will present the historic 72nd National Film Awards this evening at Ekta Nagar. Instituted in 1954, these awards represent India’s highest cinematic honours, recognising artistic and technical excellence across various categories, namely Feature, Non-Feature, and Writing on Cinema. As part of a major policy initiative by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards are being held outside the national capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar brings together cinematic talent from across the country, embodying the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. The president will also honour the veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. The stage is set, and the lights are ready in the iconic Ekta Nagar as Kevadia prepares to host the historic 72nd National Film Awards for the very first time. Renowned actors, acclaimed filmmakers, and technicians from across the country have started arriving at the venue for this grand celebration of Indian cinema. The ceremony honours outstanding cinematic achievements for the year 2024. Among the major feature film announcements, Article 370 was selected for Best Feature Film, with Yami Gautam winning Best Actress for her role in the film. The Best Actor honour is shared by Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Rajkumar Periasamy earned Best Direction for Amaran, while Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. In the non-feature category, the Marathi film Bhangaar was named Best Non-Feature Film, while Director Aanand L Rai was selected for Best Direction for Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. Ravi Raj Murmu took the Best Debut Director (Non-Feature) honour for the Santhali film, Angen.

national_raw_news.title: Sikkim’s natural farming journey reflects PM Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 7 hours ago 89
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Apart from mystic lakes and snow-capped mountains, Sikkim is famous for its vast agricultural offerings not only in India but also to the world. Sikkim has been declared the 1st Organic State in 2016 and is famous for crops like large cardamom, ginger buckwheat etc. Sikkim produces around 90% of large cardamom, which is Highest Large Cardamom in India, and exported to countries like Australia and the UAE. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Beema Yojana has played a pivotal role in the natural farming scenario in Sikkim. Apart from Large Cardamom, Buckwheat is one of the crops that’s extensively harvested in Sikkim which is around 1600kg per hector. Being the 3rd largest crop and 2nd most common cereal crop in Sikkim Buckwheat has a GI Certification. With time and with firm collaboration with Govt of India, ICAR Sikkim and Department of Agriculture, Govt of Sikkim the scene of Natural Farming as well as Organic Farming is growing stronger in Sikkim.
